questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability That a Random Variable Lies Within an Unbounded Interval
questions.problem:
Compute $P(X>1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{27}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}),\, & 0\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x>3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>1) & ={\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{4}{27}(3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{27}{\int }_{1}^{3}3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{27}{[{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{27}([(3)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(3)^{4}]-[(1)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(1)^{4}]) \\  & =\frac{4}{27}(27-\frac{81}{4}-1+\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{4}{27}\cdot 6 \\  & =\frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability That a Random Variable Lies Within an Unbounded Interval
questions.problem:
Compute $P(X\le 2)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{72}({x}^{3}+x),\, & 0\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is identical to zero for all $x<0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{72}({x}^{3}+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{72}{\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{3}+x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{72}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{72}([\frac{1}{4}(2)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}]-[\frac{1}{4}(0)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{72}(4+2-0) \\  & =\frac{6}{72} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(0\le X<1)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}{x}^{3},\, & 0\le x<2, \\ \frac{1}{5}x & 2\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X<1) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{8}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{32}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{32}({1}^{4}-{0}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(2\le X\le 3)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}({x}^{3}-x),\, & 1\le x<2, \\ \frac{1}{6}(x-1) & 2\le x\le 3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a\le X\le b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{6}(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-x]}_{2}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}([\frac{1}{2}(3)^{2}-(3)]-[\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}-2]) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{9}{2}-3-2+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{3}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Compute $P(2<X<4)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{20}\sqrt{x},\, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{20}({x}^{2}-1) & 1<x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X<4) & ={\int }_{2}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{20}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{20}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-x]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{20}([\frac{1}{3}(4)^{3}-(4)]-[\frac{1}{3}(2)^{3}-(2)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(\frac{64}{3}-4-\frac{8}{3}+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{20}(\frac{50}{3}) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
